title: An atlas of TF driven gene programs across human cells
authors: Pett JP; Prete M; Pham D; England N; Yuan H; Prigmore E; Tuck L; Oszlanczi A; To K; Xu C; Suo C; Dann E; He P; Kedlian V; Kanemaru K; Cranley J; Yang L; Elmentaite R; Oliver AJ; Cujba A; Cakir B; Murray S; Mahbubani KT; Saeb-Parsy K; Gambardella L; Kasper M; Haniffa M; Nawijn MC; Teichmann SA; Meyer KB
one_liner_zh: 该文构建人类细胞转录因子调控子图谱，基于单细胞数据关联TF与靶基因，但缺乏TF-DNA三维互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，属于广义TF调控网络分析，对本课题启发有限。
abstract: Combinations of transcription factors (TFs) regulate gene expression and determine cell fate. Much effort has been devoted to understanding TF activity in different tissues and how tissue-specificity is achieved. However, ultimately gene regulation occurs at the single cell level and the recent explosion in the availability of single cell gene expression data now makes it possible to understand TF activity at this granular level of resolution. Here, we leverage a large collection of Human Cell Atlas (HCA) single cell data to explore TF activity by examining cell-type and tissue-specific sets of target genes, or regulons. We compile a regulon atlas, CellRegulon, and map the activity of TFs in an extensive set of healthy adult and foetal tissues spanning hundreds of cell types. Using CellRegulon, we describe dynamic patterns of co-regulation, associate TF-modules with different cellular functions and characterise the distribution of active TFs and TF families across cell types. We show that CellRegulon can link disease gene expression signatures to cell types and TFs relevant to the disease. Finally, using a newly generated multiome dataset of the adult lung, we show how CellRegulon can be extended into an enhancer-gene regulatory network (eGRN) to improve cell-type associations with genetic risk loci for diseases, such as childhood onset asthma, COPD and IPF, and to identify high risk gene modules. Our database for easy download and interactive exploration allows researchers to understand key gene modules activated at cell type transitions and will therefore be valuable for tasks such as cell type engineering ( https://www.cellregulondb.org ).
abstract_zh: 转录因子（TFs）的组合调控基因表达并决定细胞命运。大量研究致力于理解不同组织中的TF活性以及组织特异性的实现方式。然而，基因调控最终发生在单细胞水平，而近年来单细胞基因表达数据的大量涌现，使得在这一精细分辨率水平上理解TF活性成为可能。在此，我们利用人类细胞图谱（HCA）单细胞数据的大规模集合，通过检查细胞类型和组织特异性的靶基因集（即调控子）来探索TF活性。我们编制了一个调控子图谱CellRegulon，并在涵盖数百种细胞类型的广泛健康成人和胎儿组织中绘制了TF活性图谱。利用CellRegulon，我们描述了共调控的动态模式，将TF模块与不同细胞功能相关联，并表征了活性TF及TF家族在细胞类型间的分布。我们展示了CellRegulon能够将疾病基因表达特征与相关细胞类型和TF联系起来。最后，利用新生成的人类成人肺多组学数据集，我们展示了如何将CellRegulon扩展为增强子-基因调控网络（eGRN），以改善与疾病（如儿童期发病哮喘、COPD和IPF）遗传风险位点的细胞类型关联，并识别高风险基因模块。我们的数据库便于下载和交互式探索，使研究人员能够理解细胞类型转变时激活的关键基因模块，因此对于细胞类型工程等任务具有重要价值（https://www.cellregulondb.org）。
